title: Forge 1: a scalar autodiff Value

wrong.overwrite_grad.py: backward closures use = instead of += (a node used twice loses a gradient path)
wrong.no_topo_order.py: backward walks the graph depth-first without a topological order (diamond graphs get partial gradients)
wrong.pow_exponent.py: d(x**n) is n * x**n instead of n * x**(n-1)
wrong.tanh_derivative.py: d tanh is 1 - t instead of 1 - t**2
wrong.relu_always_passes.py: relu passes the gradient even when the input is negative
wrong.mul_uses_own_data.py: d(a*b) multiplies by the output's own value instead of the other operand
wrong.no_seed.py: backward forgets to seed the root gradient with 1, so every grad is 0

hints: Each operation creates a new Value that remembers its inputs and a small closure _backward that pushes out.grad into the inputs' grads using the local derivative.
A node can feed several consumers, so every closure must ACCUMULATE with += (never assign). Reuse of a value is exactly why.

backward(): build a topological order of the graph with a visited set, set self.grad = 1.0, then call each node's _backward in reverse order. Division and subtraction can be built from mul, pow and neg.
